label: def:brings-coordinate-ring
title: Non-commutative coordinate ring of Bring's curve
html:
Definition. Non-commutative coordinate ring of Bring's curve

Bring's curve \mathcal{B} \subset \mathbb{P}^4 is the complete intersection

\mathcal{B}
=  V\!\bigl(
  \textstyle\sum x_i,
  \textstyle\sum x_i^2,
  \textstyle\sum x_i^3
\bigr)
\subset \mathbb{P}^4,

where [x_0 : x_1 : x_2 : x_3 : x_4] are homogeneous coordinates. This smooth algebraic curve of genus g = 4 serves as the spectral coordinate fiber of the algebraic substrate.

The non-commutative coordinate ring of \mathcal{B} is the quotient

\mathcal{O}_q(\mathcal{B})
=  \mathcal{O}_q(\mathbb{P}^4) \big/
\bigl(
  \textstyle\sum x_i,
  \textstyle\sum x_i^2,
  \textstyle\sum x_i^3
\bigr),

where \mathcal{O}_q(\mathbb{P}^4) is the quantum polynomial ring with relations x_i x_j = q x_j x_i for i < j.

The symmetric group S_5 acts on \mathcal{B} by permutation of the homogeneous coordinates. This action descends to an S_5-action on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathcal{B}) by algebra automorphisms, realizing the five-fold combinatorial symmetry of the substrate. The 2g = 8 fundamental modes of the Reeb spectrum correspond to the 8 independent cycles of \mathcal{B}, providing the spectral basis for the derivation \xi_q.
